subject: DPA: processing guardrails, subprocessors, and proof-of-control for no-training
messages:
From: Eleni Khatri <eleni@pulsehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on DPA controls & no-training proof

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for taking the time on this — PulseHealth is finalizing our procurement checklist and we need a little more detail for legal. Two core asks:

1) Contract language: Does Redwood commit to a contractual "no-training" prohibition on customer prompt/response content unless explicitly opted-in? If so, can you provide suggested clause text?

2) Proof of control: We need a concrete description of the operational controls and artifacts you can provide as evidence that customer data is not used to train models (e.g., scoped logs, retention windows, subprocessor restrictions, audit logs, or testable artifacts). A high level statement alone won't pass our InfoSec gate.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: Please confirm the list of subprocessors that touch request/response payloads, whether any learning/aggregation pipelines exist, and the mechanism for routing to EEA-only instances if we require residency.

Attached is our DPA questionnaire (Pulse_DPA_questions.xlsx). Can you review and propose a timeline for evidence delivery? Ideally we want a signed DPA + evidence package in the next 10 business days to keep the procurement timeline intact.

If it helps, we'd be happy to do a short technical call.

Best,
Eleni
Head of Procurement, PulseHealth
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Eleni Khatri <eleni@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA controls & no-training proof

Hi Eleni — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on timeline and can deliver a scoped evidence pack and suggested contract language. Quick answers up front, followed by proposed next steps: 

Short answers:
- Yes — Redwood can contractually commit to not using customer prompts/responses for model training or improvement unless a customer explicitly enables that in writing.
- Evidence we can provide: subprocessor inventory, retention/TTL configuration for request logs, a signed attestation from our operations team, and sample audit-log exports showing purge events. We will not publish training datasets derived from customer traffic.
- Subprocessor routing: we operate region-specific runtime clusters (US/EU) and can pin a customer's corpus to an EEA-only deployment. Certain managed services (e.g., cloud storage backups, logging) are handled by subprocessors; we'll provide a CSV inventory plus a mapping of which subprocessors touch payloads.

Proposed next steps:
1) Tech recap call (30 min) this week to walk through the evidence artifacts (Jonas + Dev to join).
2) We'll prepare: "redwood-no-train-explainer.pdf", a subprocessor inventory CSV, and a draft DPA clause for your review.
3) If the draft clause requires minor edits, we can iterate; if there are material asks (e.g., escrow or escrow-like exportability for outputs), we'll escalate to our enterprise legal track.

I've looped in Dev (infra) and suggest Jonas (applied ML) join the call so we can cover both operational and model-level controls. Availability: Thurs 10/15 2pm PT or Fri 10/16 11am PT. Which works?

Thanks —
Sooyjin Lee (on behalf of Redwood Privacy)
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Eleni Khatri <eleni@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Technical notes: operational controls and demonstration artifacts

Hi Eleni,

Following Soojin's note, a concise technical summary of the artifacts we can produce and what they demonstrate:

Operational controls we can evidence:
- Inference routing: customer requests are routed to dedicated or tenant-isolated runtime pools; we can show routing maps and instance IDs to demonstrate EEA-only placement.
- No-training enforcement: model weights and training pipelines are separated from inference path; by default inference logs are written to ephemeral KV cache and a short-lived request log. Training pipelines consume only explicitly provisioned training buckets — not live inference streams.
- Retention & purge: request logs default retention is configurable; for compliance customers we can set retention to X days (typically 0–90) and provide purge logs showing deletion timestamps.
- Subprocessor inventory: attached CSV (subprocessor_inventory_20261016.csv) lists subprocessors, their role (logging, object storage, monitoring), and whether they touch plaintext payloads.
- Audit exports: we can generate a signed audit export showing purge events, access control changes, and endpoint-to-instance mappings for a sample window.

Artifacts we will hand over for PulseHealth review:
- Signed operations attestation describing separation of training vs inference (PDF).
- Subprocessor inventory (CSV).
- Sample audit-log export (redacted) with SHA256 checksums and purge timestamps.
- Suggested contract text for no-training and prompt/response ownership.

A couple of practical notes:
- We do not currently provide cryptographic proof-of-non-training (e.g., zero-knowledge proofs). Evidence is operational (logs, attestations, instance mappings) plus contractual assurance. If you need an escrow-style export of all outputs, we can evaluate as a paid add-on and route to our engineering/product track.

Happy to cover these in the call — proposed time Fri 10/16 11am PT per Soojin.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
From: Eleni Khatri <eleni@pulsehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: processing guardrails, subprocessors, and proof-of-control for no-training

Soojin / Jonas,

Appreciate the quick responses and the artifact list. Our legal team reviewed the suggested approach and submitted a redline (attached Pulse_DPA_redlines.pdf). High-level asks from our side: 

- Insert explicit language that "Customer prompts and generated responses will not be used to improve models or create derivative datasets without Customer's prior written consent."
- Clarify that subprocessor inventory will be kept current and that PulseHealth will be notified of new subprocessors that can access plaintext payloads at least 30 days before onboarding.
- Require delivery of the audit export (redacted) and operations attestation as part of DPA signature.

Two questions:
1) Can Redwood accept the above as contract obligations or will you provide a different scope of commitment?
2) For EEA residency, we need a written routing map and an SLA commitment that requests will not cross regions. Is that something Redwood can include as part of the Dedicated or Private deployment offering?

We'd like to resolve this quickly to avoid procurement delay. If you can confirm acceptance of the redline items or provide counter-language by Tue 10/20 COB, we can proceed to signatures.

Best,
Eleni
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Eleni Khatri <eleni@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: processing guardrails, subprocessors, and proof-of-control for no-training

Eleni — thanks, and great to see the redlines. Short response and proposed path forward: 

1) Contract commitments: We can accept explicit "no-training without consent" language as you requested for Hosted and Dedicated contracts. For Private/on-prem we will ensure the same obligations but may include an implementation schedule where required by deployment specifics. We'll propose exact clause text in the next hour via DocuSign-ready draft.

2) Subprocessor notice: We can commit to a 30-day notice for any subprocessor that will handle plaintext customer payloads. We'll include a mechanism for PulseHealth to request targeted attestation for any new subprocessor.

3) Evidence deliverables: We will include the operations attestation and a redacted audit export with the signed DPA. The audit export will include purge timestamps and instance routing metadata for a sample 7-day window.

4) EEA residency SLA: EEA-only routing is available on Dedicated and Private plans. We can include contractual routing maps and an availability/latency SLA; because this requires capacity reservation, we'll attach an appendix for Dedicated capacity pricing. If you'd like, I can loop our Dedicated sales lead for pricing in parallel.

Next steps:
- I'll send a DocuSign draft with the agreed clauses and attach the redwood-no-train-explainer.pdf and the subprocessor CSV.
- If the clause set looks good, please sign and we'll ship the attestation + sample audit export within 3 business days of signature.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcdef-2026-10
HubSpot (deal): https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/8247

If you want the supplemental technical artifacts ahead of signature for legal review, let me know and we'll provision them to a secure share.

Thanks,
Sooyin Lee
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
